findings.location: Section 7.4.3, p.69, geometric plate assertion and (7.12); (7.15), (7.20)-(7.23), pp.69-71
findings.claim: Moving x outside the minimal concentration plane V is asserted to make every hyperplane through x transverse to V, giving nu_Z(H^(delta))=O(m^-2).
findings.evidence: Fixed d=4 measures on separated polynomial graph patches F_*(u,v)=(u,v,1+u^2,v^2), F_j(u,v)=(u,v,a_j+e_j u^2,e_j v^2), a_j=1/(j+2), e_j=2^(-4j), rho=1/10, weights 1/[j(j+1)]. All are uniformly 2-Frostman, have finite s-energy for s<2, and give every hyperplane zero mass. Radial projections of every F_j patch from every F_* pin have uniformly bounded inverse charts and hence 2-thin tubes. At m_j=2j, Y=F_j(square) has nu(Y)>m_j^-2 and the minimal concentration dimension is 2. H=aff(V_j,x) contains V_j and x and intersects Y, while all Y is within delta=2^(-epsilon_prime*m_j) of H. Thus nu_Z(H^(delta))=1 at arbitrarily large m_j, also violating the angular estimate.
findings.impact: The entropy branch using Lemma 3.11 in the proof of Theorem 1.3 lacks its required hypothesis. No counterexample to the theorem itself is claimed.
findings.repair_limit: Transversality to every relevant H cannot follow from x outside V when dim V<=d-2. A different concentration/dimension-reduction argument is required; no complete repair established. Fixing the separately incorrect printed exponent ratio does not repair geometry.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: The disputed step must hold for the fixed Frostman measures with separated supports, qualitative hyperplane non-concentration and strong thin tubes, at every sufficiently large allowed m and for every retained Y with nu(Y)>m^-2. It cannot be refuted solely by an isolated exceptional pin or by measures changed with m.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Fix d=4, Q=[-1/10,1/10]^2, F*(u,v)=(u,v,1+u^2,v^2), Fj(u,v)=(u,v,aj+ej*u^2,ej*v^2), aj=1/(j+2), ej=2^(-4j), and weights wj=1/[j(j+1)]. The weights telescope to one. The compact support includes the limit plane patch and has Hausdorff and packing dimension two. The first two coordinates yield uniform 2-Frostman bounds, hence finite s-energy for every s<2. Every nonzero affine hyperplane functional restricts to a nonzero polynomial in 1,u,v,u^2,v^2 on each graph (the coefficient determinant uses ej^2>0), so every hyperplane has zero mass. The supports are separated. Common translation/dilation, if a bounded-box normalization is needed, preserves these properties and the contradiction up to fixed constants.
acceptance_check.strong_tube_and_uniformity_check: For x in supp(mu), use the gnomonic coordinates g1=(u-x1)/D and g2=(v-x2)/D, D=x3-aj-ej*u^2. Here D>=2/3-1/1600 and D<=1.01. The numerator of dg1/du is at least 2/3-1/800; g1 is strictly increasing and g2 is affine in v. The inverse chart is uniformly Lipschitz on every patch, independently of j and x. Thus radial masses of balls are O(r^2), uniformly for the entire fixed mixture, stronger than the required exponent s4<2. One may take all Yx=supp(nu), so the full product is compact.
acceptance_check.scale_witness: At mj=2j and delta=2^(-epsilon_prime*mj), choose Y=Fj(Q). Then nu(Y)=wj>mj^-2 and nu_Y=nu_j. Uniform point and line tube estimates O(delta^2), O(delta) eventually fall below the k=0,1 concentration thresholds mj^-10,mj^-8, whereas the plane Vj={(u,v,aj,0)} has mass one in its delta-neighborhood. Hence the minimal k is two and Z=Y. For every pin x in supp(mu), H=aff(Vj,x) is a hyperplane through x containing Vj; its normal may be taken as (0,0,-x4,x3-aj). On Fj(Q) the affine functional is ej[-x4*u^2+(x3-aj)*v^2], so distance to H is at most sqrt(2)*ej/100, much smaller than delta. Thus nu_Z(H^(delta))=1 at arbitrarily large scales, not O(m^-2). Infinitely many mj are divisible by any previously fixed T. The separation lets c_epsilon be chosen with no pin removed; here G and A retain every pin. This is not a null-pin exception.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: Qualitative zero hyperplane mass does not imply the uniform small-scale conditional estimate after restriction to Z. A hyperplane through x can contain V when dim V<=d-2, so x outside V does not supply the asserted transversality. The printed exponent ratio is separately m^2; changing that arithmetic, or using the threshold for k-1, cannot remove the geometric obstruction. The constructed smooth patches are not counterexamples to a distance-set theorem; another choice of Frostman measure would not validate the stated universal intermediate step.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: The failed (7.12)/(7.15) supplies the hypothesis for Lemma 3.11 in (7.20), then (7.21)-(7.23) in the proof of Theorem 1.3. This is a core proof defect for the lower box estimate in that branch, not an established falsity of Theorem 1.3, Theorem 1.4, or a Hausdorff-distance conclusion.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: A different concentration/transversality or dimension-reduction argument is needed. No complete repair of this branch is established. The report's Major classification and explicit theorem-level limit are retained.

findings.location: Lemma 6.5 and preceding fiber identities, p.51; Theorem 6.6 density identity, p.52; Figures 3-4
findings.claim: An oriented cylindrical slice is identified with a full affine-plane slice and asserted mutually absolutely continuous to it; the full-plane slice mass is then identified with an oriented angular density.
findings.evidence: d=k=2, x=0, nu=16*Lebesgue on [1/4,1/2] x [-1/8,1/8], theta=-e1. The oriented slice is zero, but the full-line slice has mass 4. The corresponding integrated full-line measure has oriented angular density 8 at +e1 and 0 at -e1, whereas the printed identity gives 4 at both.
findings.impact: The printed central disintegration proof contains a false mutual absolute-continuity step and a false density identity. This is a proof issue, not a counterexample to the desired integrated comparison or final distance results.
findings.repair_limit: Compare the full-plane slice to the sum of the two antipodal cylindrical slices; integrate both and use the antipodal L^p bound. Tube intersections use two caps. This supplies a bounded repair of the orientation step, while retaining external radial-projection inputs.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: The radial map is explicitly oriented, pi_x(y)=(y-x)/|y-x|, and (6.3) uses one sphere cap. Full orthogonal line/plane slices contain both directions. The d=k=2 example obeys the separation and finiteness assumptions. It persists on angular intervals; a smooth pin measure near zero supplies admissible finite s-energy for 1<s<2 when a positive set of pins is required.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: Let nu=16 Lebesgue measure on [1/4,1/2] x [-1/8,1/8], x=0. At theta=-e1 the oriented cylindrical slice is zero, but the horizontal full-line slice has mass 16*(1/2-1/4)=4. At +e1 the cylindrical mass is 16*integral_(1/4)^(1/2) r dr=3/2. Under the source's normalizations, the full-line integral Lambda over S^1 satisfies dLambda=2/|y| dnu, so its oriented pushforward has density 8 at +e1 and zero at -e1, whereas the printed full-plane mass identity gives four at both. The failure is stable for a nonzero angular neighborhood, not just one null direction.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The earlier two-to-one identification of G(V,1) with the sphere was explicitly considered. It makes unoriented orthogonal projection notation convenient but does not change the explicitly oriented pi_x or the one-cap denominator in (6.3). Figures 3 and 4 and the source images were checked; the full plane drawn for the fiber does not cure the inconsistent oriented definition.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: Lemma 6.5's mutual absolute continuity and the density equality in Theorem 6.6 are false as written; they are central to the slicing/disintegration argument used by Theorem 6.7. Major denotes an invalid core derivation. Neither the desired integrated comparability nor the final distance theorem has been disproved.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Compare each full slice with the sum of the two antipodal cylindrical slices, using bounded radial weights from separation and bounded support. Integrating the sum gives 2nu. If f is the oriented density, the correct bound is by C(f(theta)+f(-theta)); (a+b)^p<=2^(p-1)(a^p+b^p) preserves the L^p estimate and the external radial-projection input. In the Theorem 6.7 tail on pp.55-56 use two caps; their measure remains O(r^k), preserving the r^(k+t) power. This is a bounded orientation repair, not independent reproof of all external projection results.

findings.claim: Generic box slice dimension is bounded by min(dim_B E-k,0).
findings.evidence: E=[-1,1]^3, k=1: the positive-measure family of planes cutting the interior has two-dimensional sections, whereas min(3-1,0)=0.
findings.impact: False displayed bound; later applications use the intended positive dimension difference rather than zero.
findings.repair_limit: Replace min with max (with the empty-slice convention). A direct cover/Markov/Borel-Cantelli argument gives the corrected generic upper bound.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: A bounded Borel E and k in {1,...,d-1}; the claim is for affine (d-k)-planes almost everywhere with respect to the stated affine-plane measure.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: For E=[-1,1]^3 and k=1, a positive-measure family of planes cuts its interior in a two-dimensional section, contradicting the printed upper bound min(3-1,0)=0. For the repair, cover a bounded E at dyadic scale r using at most C*r^(-D-epsilon) cubes, D=upper box dimension. The expected number met by a random translate of a (d-k)-plane is O(r^(k-D-epsilon)). Markov at r^(-D+k-2epsilon) gives a summable dyadic exceptional probability. Hence the generic upper bound is D-k for D>=k; for D<k, almost every slice is empty; D=k gives at most zero dimension.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The following application already uses a positive dimension difference (p.62), not the printed minimum with zero. Empty-slice conventions must be stated at the D<k endpoint.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: False extremum in a displayed ancillary slicing lemma, with the intended generic bound supplied by the direct cover argument and used correctly afterwards.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Replace min by max under the empty-slice convention. Retain Minor; this does not repair P1 or establish unrelated quantitative restrictions.

findings.location: Proposition 5.17 proof (5.15), p.47; normalized profile in Section 7.4.6, p.70; compare p.26
findings.claim: The induction uses a f(x/a) on [0,1]; the later dimension profile omits 1/ell.
findings.evidence: For every actual 0<a<=1/2, a f(x/a) requires f beyond its stated domain for x>a. The correct dilation is f(a x)/a, preserving slopes and scaling interval lengths by a. For d=4, ell=8 and beta_i=2, the p.70 profile has f(1)=16 and slope16, contradicting its claimed range/Lipschitz bound4; dividing by ell gives f(1)=2 and slope2, as already printed on p.26.
findings.impact: Local normalization errors prevent literal application of the stated combinatorial class; the explicit corrections preserve the intended scale argument.
findings.repair_limit: Use f(a x)/a and sum(beta)/ell. This does not repair P1 or certify all omitted constant bookkeeping.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: The induction parameter has 0<a<=1/2 and the admissible function is defined on [0,1], with the stated Lipschitz, lower-envelope and interval constraints.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: The printed a*f(x/a) is undefined for x>a in [0,1]. Setting g(x)=f(a*x)/a keeps the domain, slope bound, monotonicity, origin and lower-envelope condition. A superlinear interval [A,B] for g scales to [aA,aB] for f, including the allowable interval threshold and its factor a in (5.15). Separately, with d=4, ell=8 and every beta_i=2, the p.70 unnormalized profile has f(1)=16 and slope16, incompatible with range [0,4] and 4-Lipschitzness. Dividing the partial sums by ell gives f(1)=2 and slope2, exactly the earlier normalization on p.26.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: These are domain/normalization errors with explicit valid corrected scalings. They are not evidence that all constant bookkeeping or the separate concentration step has been repaired.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: Local literal failures in applying the established combinatorial class; the intended scaling structure is preserved after correction.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Use f(a*x)/a and partial sums divided by ell. Minor retained; P1 remains separately unresolved at the proof-repair level.

findings.claim: The projected probability measure is declared robust with mass threshold delta^(-eta), followed by a nonvacuous adaptedness assertion.
findings.evidence: For 0<delta<1 and eta>0 the threshold exceeds1, so no probability-measurable set satisfies the triggering condition. At delta=2^-16, eta=1/4 the threshold is16.
findings.impact: The printed robustness clause is vacuous and does not furnish the advertised implication.
findings.repair_limit: A positive mass exponent is needed. The stronger discretized projection theorem must be invoked in that nonvacuous form; the sign correction is not itself a new proof of the cited theorem.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: Definition 2.2 tests sets with probability mass greater than the robustness parameter. The lemma has 0<delta<1 and eta>0.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: delta^(-eta)>1, so no set of a probability measure triggers the displayed robustness condition. For delta=2^-16 and eta=1/4 the threshold is16. The clause is therefore vacuously true, rather than a false stand-alone assertion, and cannot by itself provide the following nonvacuous adaptedness conclusion.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The source explicitly appeals to a stronger external discretized projection theorem. Its independent proof was not supplied by changing a sign, and the present check does not pretend otherwise.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: The displayed threshold loses the intended meaning/implication. The report correctly distinguishes vacuity from a counterexample to the external theorem.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: A positive mass exponent in the appropriate nonvacuous form of the cited theorem is needed. Retain Minor and the external-dependency limitation; no external result is newly certified.

findings.claim: Each dyadic cube is said to meet O_d(a^d) joint-partition atoms, and this is used for the reverse conditional entropy.
findings.evidence: The factor tends to zero although a cube meeting the partition meets at least one atom; the conditional entropy needs the number of dyadic cubes per joint atom. For rows (1,0), (sqrt(1-a^2),a), a joint atom has area 2^(-2m)/a and crosses order a^-1 dyadic squares.
findings.impact: The displayed justification for the entropy inequality has the wrong direction and exponent; the lemma's conclusion survives a corrected cover argument.
findings.repair_limit: The projection matrix has determinant at least a^(d-1). Each joint atom meets O_d(a^(-(d-1))) dyadic cubes, hence at most O_d(a^-d), giving the stated d log(1/a)+O_d(1) conditional entropy loss.

acceptance_check.hypotheses_and_quantifiers: 0<a<=1 and successively transverse unit directions. The entropy to bound is H(D_m | D_m'), so its fibers are dyadic cubes inside a fixed joint-partition atom.
acceptance_check.independent_argument: O_d(a^d) tends to zero while a nonempty cube meets at least one atom. The printed incidence direction is also reversed. For rows (1,0),(sqrt(1-a^2),a), the joint cell area is 2^(-2m)/a, showing the inverse growth. In general Gram-Schmidt gives |det A|>=a^(d-1). The union of dyadic cubes meeting a joint atom lies in that atom enlarged by one bounded cube; applying A bounds the image volume by C_d*2^(-dm), since all rows have norm one. Division by the determinant bounds the number of cubes by C_d*a^(-(d-1))<=C_d*a^-d. Therefore H(D_m|D_m')<=d log(1/a)+O_d(1), as needed.
acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_boundary: The lemma's entropy conclusion survives this corrected cover argument. The counterexample targets the stated justification, not the existence of the selected directions or the final inequality.
acceptance_check.dependency_and_impact: Wrong exponent and incidence direction in a local justification with a complete corrected bound. Minor retained.
acceptance_check.repair_and_limit: Count dyadic cubes per joint atom with an inverse power of a. The correction does not supply the missing hypothesis for P1's later application.

independent_acceptance.scope: Focused independent acceptance of the frozen reported Problems, including Minor subfindings, evidence and honest coverage. This is not a new whole-paper initial review or a search for unrelated defects.

native_auxiliary_attribution.scope: Bounded read-only challenge of P1/P2 hypotheses, fixed-measure and positive-pin witnesses, orientation repair and downstream scope; source text only, no writes, viewing or build.
native_auxiliary_attribution.role_in_decision: Advisory cross-check. The primary executor independently checked all six Problems, source pages and mathematical arguments.

independent_acceptance.boundary_statement: The 74-page author preprint is retained exactly; neither the arXiv page-count comment nor the 76-page journal pagination establishes version equivalence. No main distance-set conclusion is declared false. External theorems and the absence of a full repair for Section 7.4 remain explicit limitations. No author code was run; existing bounded supplement/code/erratum searches are reused only at their recorded scope.
